output.brief:
The fall in incidents is not real. Since 9 September, a script on a Brackwater analyst host has checked every five minutes for confirmed incidents that are close to breaching the 4-hour containment deadline. It then moved 47 of them (23 in September, 24 in October) into the "Suspicious Activity–Monitoring" category. Each had already been confirmed by an analyst, and none had a containment timestamp. Moving them removes them from the containment and SLA statistics. That is why Brackwater reports 100% on time and why the monitoring queue has grown. About 36 to 37 incidents a month are still being confirmed, the same as before. The platform connector made no category changes, so this is not a software fault. The evidence shows someone using Brackwater's access did this. It does not show who decided to, or why. I did not check whether the 28 dropped detection rules are hiding attacks. That remains open.

What to do before Thursday:
- Do not cut the Halvard retainer.
- Do not pay the 60k bonus.
- Reinstate the 47 cases and have Corvane's team and Halvard verify containment on each.
- Remove category-edit rights from the Brackwater integration role.
- Ask Brackwater for a written explanation.
- Hold off on service-credit claims until the contract has been reviewed.
